chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'A'la, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about urine that hits the body. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Pour water upon it twice.' And it is reported that it suffices to wash with an equal amount of water if it is on the tip of the foreskin and other parts. And it is reported that it is water, not filth, so it needs to be rubbed.
ai.seo_question: How to purify urine stains on the body according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the baseline method for purifying urine stains on the body, emphasizing the sufficiency of pouring water twice. It further contextualizes the ruling by distinguishing between thick filth (hathafah), which requires washing, and thinner urine, which may only require rubbing, reflecting the Shia juristic debate on the definition of 'filth' and the practical ease of purification.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’ala who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the urine hitting the body. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Pour the water upon it, twice’. 
And it is reported that it would suffice him if he were to wash with the likes of it from the water when it was upon the tip of the manhood. And it is reported that it is water and not filth, so it needs to be rubbed.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Al-Husayn ibn abu al-‘Ala’ who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about urine which pollutes the body. He (the Imam) said, Tour water on it twice.’ It is a narration that one can wash it with the same amount of water if it is on the tip of the penis or on something else. It also is a narration that it is water and not dirt and it needs to be dropped down.’”
